clues: Hattie's float rolled exactly two floats ahead of Arlo's.
Hattie rode either at the very front of the parade or at the very back.
Selma rode on the float right in front of Arlo's.
hints: Look at Hattie's row, where clue 2 allows only two places. Do both of them work with clue 1?
Put clues 1 and 2 together: clue 1 needs room behind Hattie for Arlo, two floats back. Which end of the parade has room behind it?
Nothing rolled behind the last float, so Hattie led the parade. Then by clue 1, Arlo rode on the third float.

solution.key_idea: Clue 1 needs room behind Hattie, so of clue 2's two ends she took the front, and Arlo rode third.
steps: By clue 2, Hattie rode on the first float or the fourth.
By clue 1, Arlo rode two floats behind Hattie, and no float came behind the fourth, so Hattie rode on the first float.
Then by clue 1, Arlo rode on the third float.
By clue 3, Selma rode right in front of Arlo, so Selma rode on the second float.
That leaves the fourth float, at the very back, for Nico and his lobster.
solution.epilogue: The correction box ran on Monday: Hattie first, then Selma, Arlo and Nico. Nico's lobster brought up the rear, and by Tuesday it was the size of two canoes.

tip: An exact gap needs room. Before you put someone at an end, check that the gap still fits.
